text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000086 bills 99215 well above expectation in every complexity tier, including low-complexity visits, but only a handful of charts have been reviewed, too few to confirm or rule out upcoding.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The elevated 99215 share holds even after risk adjustment and appears in every complexity tier, roughly double the all-provider share at each level, so a sicker panel does not fully explain it; the heavy 99214 concentration in the mix points the same way. The sampled low-complexity 99215 claims are the main concern: several are for self-limited problems such as upper respiratory infection (C0049062, C0049251), rash (C0049524, C0050382) and urinary tract infection (C0049421, C0050064), which rarely support high-complexity decision-making. The high-complexity samples, by contrast, look consistent with the billed level, and C0049452 is documented as high MDM. The documentation is too thin to judge: only about 1% of claims have records, there is one unsupported 99215 (C0049179, documented moderate), and the 99214 unsupported rate looks high but rests on 11 charts. The two moderate-plus data-reviewed notes without a lab or test line are weak evidence of templated notes, not proof. A reviewer should first request charts for the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims and a larger 99214 sample, and check whether the notes are cloned or templated."}
